summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, independently_verified=false). Studio did not run; simulation status is 'skipped' because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, and the extracted floorplan is empty. The final verdict is gated off, simulation_allowed=false and comparison_valid=false. The selected scenario is the inline (IA) circular pin-fin aluminium heat sink with 36 fins cooling a single 2.2 x 2.2 x 0.1 cm chip at a constant 8 W. It is a 3D steady conjugate CFD (ANSYS Icepak/FLUENT) with 0.1 m/s inlet air at 298 K in a 6 x 5 x 2 cm cabinet with adiabatic walls. This is a custom 2D steady request, so there is no transient trace. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration. It involves no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes and powers, and no source commit is available. No illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was produced, and no placement assumption was used because the paper gives no block coordinates. The paper reports a maximum source temperature of 126.97 C (Table 6, PDF p.11), a spatial maximum from a steady 3D forced-convection solution. No Studio temperature exists, so no numerical comparison is made or valid. Even if Studio had run, the location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions would not match: the paper has 3D airflow over pin fins, while Studio would be a 2D conduction model. The result gives only a qualitative statement: a conduction-only 2D model cannot capture the airflow-driven pin-fin cooling that sets this temperature. No exact replication is claimed. The decision rests on essential physical mismatches, missing placement and inconsistent geometry, and the gate output, not on a simulated result.

The setup is a 3D conjugate CFD model with forced air convection through an enclosed cabinet (0.1 m/s inlet, pressure outlet, insulated walls). It has no chiplets, interposer or 3D stack, and a steady 2D conduction-only Studio model cannot represent the 3D airflow, fin geometry, pressure drop or velocity fields.

The cooling is a 36-pin aluminium finned heat sink with air flow. A bundled Studio package/material stack does not include these pin fins or the airflow, so the cooling path and boundary conditions differ essentially.

The paper's dimensions are internally inconsistent: Table 1 gives a 4 x 4 x 1.7 cm heat sink and a 0.2 cm fin diameter, while the text gives a 3 x 3.5 x 2 cm base, 1.5 cm fin height and 0.16 cm fin radius. The geometry is ambiguous.

The paper contains no block placement coordinates. Only the chip footprint, the heat sink and cabinet sizes, and a single 8 W power are published, so any 2D placement would be an illustrative construction and not paper-derived.
The paper runs a steady-state analysis with a constant 8 W load. It provides no transient power trace, no controller and no optimizer, so any one-row power trace is not a published workload.

The paper reports a maximum chip temperature of 126.97 C with 298 K inlet air and a 0.1 m/s flow rate. It assumes constant material properties and neglects radiation and gravity. Studio temperatures cannot be compared numerically with this value.

Table 3 and the boundary-condition text are ambiguous about where the heat is applied, whether to the heat sink bottom wall or the chip, and about an unspecified substrate board. Reported mesh sizes and solver details (Table 4) do not map to a Studio solver.

Bundled Studio package/material assumptions are not specified in the supplied packet and are not paper-derived; they would be a separate 2D conduction model with its own package and material properties.
A runner may construct a separate illustrative 2D placement of the 2.2 x 2.2 cm chip footprint with 8 W and a one-row power trace; such coordinates are generated and not paper facts.
Studio temperatures must not be compared numerically with the paper's 126.97 C value.
No exact replication is claimed. No floorplan blocks are asserted as paper-derived, because no placement coordinates exist.
